correctness.rationale: Every step of the infinite theorem has a self-contained combinatorial proof: domination iff all rows or all columns occupied; complement-total iff no row-column cross contains the set; nonoverlapping a>=3 row-obstruction cases and special a=2 case; inclusion-exclusion and explicitly unique deficient intersection crosses for all but 2x2; sharp lower bounds, constructions, and exact classified minima. Exhaustive direct-adjacency tests of 271,904 minimum-sized-or-smaller subsets and 1,435,472 full-cardinality subsets passed. The finite tests are supplementary, not the infinite argument.

evidence: For \(3\le m<n\), known ordinary rook domination has \(n^m\) minimum-size row transversals; the mixed invariant counts \(n^m-n-mn(n-1)\) admissible minimum row transversals.
The elementary cross obstruction is absent from the ordinary rook theorem and additional work proves the new exclusion count and the all-size correction.
Bermudo et al., 2024, propose the mixed parameter but do not derive its rook polynomial.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The prior ordinary cardinality polynomial strictly counts a superset and does not give the exact cross-contained subsets without new reasoning. The founding mixed parameter work gives neither this family classification nor the needed all-size enumerator; no inspected stronger statement subsumes the claim.

evidence: Rook graph is the line graph of the complete bipartite graph, hence equivalent to nonattacking row-column occupancy language.
For a selected rook set, complement-total domination means it is not contained in any row-column cross; this is strictly stronger than ordinary domination.
Full-text check of arXiv:2401.00716 yields the ordinary rook polynomial only.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The placement and line-graph descriptions were included in searches. Unlike standard global domination (ordinary domination in both graphs), the mixed condition demands complement-neighbors for selected vertices too. No searched equivalence with a pre-existing full count was identified.

evidence: Mertens, arXiv:2401.00716, Theorem and enumerative tables give ordinary domination, not complement-total domination.
OEIS total-domination data for rook graphs concern total domination in the original rook graph, rather than its complement.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: A known table of ordinary dominating sets permits coefficientwise comparisons but does not enforce the new open-neighborhood complement condition. A table of total dominating rook placements is a different parameter, so neither is an exact table of the mixed invariant.

originality.rationale: The original 2024 parameter introduction discusses modular graph products; the 2024 full-text rook domination paper studies only ordinary domination. Explicit row-column cross obstructions and the complete mixed polynomial, including minimum multiplicities, are not implied by those results; a bounded search found no identified stronger covering result. Unindexed and inaccessible literature remain residual risks.
residual_risks: Unindexed or differently named results may already contain the mixed rook-graph cardinality polynomial.
The full texts of two plausible older broad simultaneous/complement-parameter articles were not accessible; their abstracts were compared only.
Neither independent scientific review nor external validation has been performed.

value.rationale: The recently introduced mixed domination invariant has natural unresolved exact families; the two-dimensional rook graph is a canonical product of complete graphs. A complete all-cardinality polynomial and full optimizer classification add new structural cross exclusions beyond the known ordinary rook domination polynomial. The m=2 boundary and exact multiplicity formulas have natural combinatorial meaning and are applicable without numerical computation.
